findings.title: Empty `data: {}` update is unlikely to bump `updatedAt`, and nothing reads that timestamp
findings.description:
`fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` to "Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt". Two problems:

- **The write probably does nothing.** `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is `DateTime? @updatedAt` (`schema.prisma:860`). As far as I recall, Prisma only injects `@updatedAt` when the update payload is non-empty, so `{}` is a no-op. I did not run this against a database. Either pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` explicitly or add a test that pins the behaviour.
- **The value is never consumed.** The UI's "Last updated" comes from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` via `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, which the upsert in `upsertCachedAvailability` already bumps. The new `updatedAt`/`googleChannelId` selects in `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts:899-900` and the widened `UserWithCalendars` type have no readers in `getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts`.

So this adds a credential-wide `updateMany` on every Google webhook, plus two extra columns on every session-user load (`findUnlockedUserForSession`), for no observable effect. Remove it, or wire it to an actual consumer.

findings.title: `updateManyByCredentialId` takes the wrong Prisma input type
findings.description: The parameter is typed `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`, which is the single-record type and includes nested relation writes (`user`, `credential`, `eventType`). `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany` does not support those. Because the argument is not a fresh literal, a caller could pass relation fields that compile and then fail at runtime. Use `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput` (or the unchecked variant).

findings.title: Cache status stays stale after "Delete cached data" where no `onChanged` is passed
findings.description:
`deleteCacheMutation.onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls `onSuccess?.()`. Unlike `disconnectMutation`, whose `onSettled` invalidates `connectedCalendars` and `integrations`, it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`.

- `CalendarListContainer.tsx:79-88` passes an `onChanged` that invalidates, so that page refreshes.
- `EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-384` passes no `onChanged`, so the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated" and the delete action after the cache is gone.

Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` inside the component, as the disconnect mutation does.

findings.title: `connectedCalendars` handler bypasses the `calendar-cache` feature flag, leaving the new mock method unused
findings.description:
The handler instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init(...)` (`calendar-cache.ts:22-29`), which returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the feature is globally disabled. Consequences:

- `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` has no caller.
- With the flag off, leftover cache rows still surface a cache status and delete action in the UI.
- Every `connectedCalendars` query now issues an extra `groupBy`, including for users with no Google credential or an empty `credentialIds` list.

Route through `CalendarCache.init(null)` and short-circuit when there are no Google credential ids.

findings.title: `deleteCacheHandler` throws a plain `Error` and bypasses the repository layer
findings.description:
- **Error type.** `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` surfaces to clients as `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (500) for what is a not-found/forbidden condition. The sibling `setDestinationCalendar.handler.ts:77` uses `TRPCError` with an explicit code.
- **Layering.** The handler calls `prisma.credential.findFirst` and `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` directly. The same diff adds a read method to `ICalendarCacheRepository`, and the mock already has a `deleteManyByCredential` stub that is not on the interface. The delete belongs on the repository.
- **Schema placement.** The input schema is inlined in `_router.tsx:29` rather than in a `deleteCache.schema.ts` like the sibling procedures.

The ownership check itself (`userId: user.id`) is correct.

findings.title: Disconnect is now hidden for broken connections when `disableConnectionModification` is set
findings.description:
The error/`Alert` branch previously gated the disconnect button only on `!connectedCalendar.delegationCredentialId`. It now passes `disableConnectionModification` into `CredentialActionsDropdown`, where `canDisconnect` requires it to be false. `EventAdvancedTab.tsx:375` sets it to `true`, so a broken calendar connection can no longer be removed from that screen. If intentional, say so; otherwise keep the old gating for the error branch.

Two related side effects of the same refactor:
- On that same tab, a Google credential with cache now exposes the credential-wide "Delete cached data" action, although connection modification is meant to be disabled there.
- The `<div className="flex w-32 justify-end">` wrapper is always rendered, even when the dropdown returns `null`, reserving empty space where there was none.

findings.title: No tests for any of the new behaviour
findings.description:
A search of `*.test.*` / `*.spec.*` files finds no references to `deleteCache`, `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, `updateManyByCredentialId`, or `CredentialActionsDropdown`. Gaps that matter:

- The authorization path of `deleteCacheHandler` (another user's credential must be rejected). The same directory already has `setDestinationCalendar.handler.test.ts` as a pattern.
- The `_max(updatedAt)` aggregation in `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`.
- The `updatedAt` bump in `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`. The existing tests at `CalendarService.test.ts:664` and `:733` would be the place, and would settle the empty-data question above.

findings.title: Dev script is macOS-only, CWD-dependent, and reports success on failure
findings.description:
- **Line 70:** `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD syntax. On GNU sed the `''` is taken as the script and the substitution as a filename, so it fails. The script still prints "✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL" because there is no `set -e` or status check.
- **Line 5:** `ENV_FILE="../.env"` resolves against the caller's working directory. Run from the repo root, it creates or edits a `.env` outside the repository. Resolve from `$(dirname "$0")` instead.
- **Lines 11-18:** `cleanup` always does `exit 0`, so the rate-limit and "Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL" paths exit successfully.
- **Lines 28-31:** when reusing a running `tmole`, the URL is read from `/tmp/tmole.log`, which may be missing or stale from an earlier session.
- **Name:** the file is called `test-…` but only starts a tunnel and rewrites an env var. Nothing references it from `package.json`, docs or other scripts.

findings.title: Disconnect logic duplicated from `DisconnectIntegration`
findings.description: The `trpc.viewer.credentials.delete` mutation (toasts, `onSettled` invalidations) is copied from `DisconnectIntegration.tsx:26-40` rather than shared, so the two will drift. The copy already drops the `teamId` forwarding and the `isDelegationCredential({ credentialId })` guard. Extract a shared hook. The file also has two separate imports from `@calcom/ui/components/dialog` (lines 9-10).

findings.title: UI conventions in `CredentialActionsDropdown`
findings.description:
- The timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded `"en-US"` locale rather than the user's locale from `useLocale()`.
- Raw palette classes (`text-gray-900 dark:text-white`, `text-gray-500 dark:text-white`) are used instead of the semantic tokens (`text-emphasis`, `text-subtle`) used elsewhere in the wrapper.
- The read-only "Cache Status" block is rendered as a `DropdownMenuItem`, so it is focusable and selectable, and clicking it closes the menu. A label or plain container would be more appropriate.
- The icon-only trigger button has no accessible label.
- `hasCache` evaluates to `"" | Date | null | undefined | false` rather than a boolean; `Boolean(...)` is safer for JSX `&&`.

findings.title: Migration header contradicts the SQL; backfilled timestamps are synthetic
findings.description: The auto-generated warning says the column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the statement adds `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`. Drop the stale warning. Existing cache rows will show the migration time as "Last updated" until they are next refreshed. The schema's `@default(now()) @updatedAt` matches the migration.

findings.title: Ownership check on `deleteCache`, and type widening is compatible with other callers
findings.description:
- The mutation is behind `authedProcedure` and scopes the credential lookup to `userId: user.id` before deleting, so one user cannot purge another's cache.
- The widened `UserWithCalendars` type is still satisfied by API v1 (`findManyByIdsIncludeDestinationAndSelectedCalendars` uses `include: { selectedCalendars: true }`) and API v2 (`findByIdWithCalendars` likewise).
- All new i18n keys exist in `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json` (lines 1382-1386, 3381-3387).
- `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TYPE` resolves to `"google_calendar"` in `packages/platform/constants/apps.ts:1`.

structured_findings.summary: Empty `data: {}` update is unlikely to bump `updatedAt`, and nothing reads that timestamp
`updateManyByCredentialId` takes the wrong Prisma input type

`connectedCalendars` handler bypasses the `calendar-cache` feature flag, leaving the new mock method unused
`deleteCacheHandler` throws a plain `Error` and bypasses the repository layer
Disconnect is now hidden for broken connections when `disableConnectionModification` is set
No tests for any of the new behaviour
Dev script is macOS-only, CWD-dependent, and reports success on failure
Migration header contradicts the SQL; backfilled timestamps are synthetic
Ownership check on `deleteCache`, and type widening is compatible with other callers
